businessRules.rule: A payment above the limit needs a second approver.
businessRules.enforcedBy: an API guard on the server route

asIs: Payments are approved by email and nobody can tell afterwards who approved which one.

delta: Approval moves from email to the product, so who approved what is recorded rather than remembered.

problem.statement: Nobody can say afterwards who approved a payment, so every audit becomes a reconstruction.
problem.metric: share of payments with a named approver recorded at the time
problem.baselineMeasuredBy: the settlement database, counting approvals with a null actor

guardrails.metric: median time to approve a payment

problem.counterEvidence: If the audit team already reconstructs approvals from email in under an hour, this is not worth building.
problem.hmw: How might we make who approved what recoverable after the fact?

concepts.approach: a queue the approver works down, newest last
concepts.why: kept: it is the only shape that shows how long the oldest item has waited

concepts.approach: approval inside the payment record itself
concepts.why: it hides how many are waiting, which is the number the fraud analyst needs first

changeControl: Any addition is priced as a change order and moves the date by the same number of days.

segments.name: branch approver
segments.jobToBeDone: release a held payment without leaving the queue
segments.context: at a desk, on a shared terminal, interrupted every few minutes
segments.fluency: high in the product, low in anything else

segments.name: compliance director
segments.jobToBeDone: answer an inspection without a reconstruction project
segments.context: at a desk, alone, under a deadline set by somebody else
segments.frequency: twice a quarter and once in anger
segments.shortfallWhy: three people hold this role in the whole bank and all three were interviewed. This is the population, not a sample of it, and the shortfall against five cannot be closed

painPoints.statement: I can see it was approved but not who approved it.
painPoints.workaround: search the mailbox by date and hope the thread survived

painPoints.statement: The queue does not tell me which one has been waiting longest.
painPoints.workaround: sort by reference and infer the order from it
painPoints.costs: the oldest item is released last about a third of the time

painPoints.statement: I approve things I cannot really check.
painPoints.workaround: call the originating branch when the amount looks unusual

saidNo.who: a regional bank that evaluated the product and kept its spreadsheet
saidNo.why: the spreadsheet already had the audit columns and nobody would own a migration

competitors.packaging: everything or nothing, negotiated per bank
competitors.positioning: the safe option nobody is fired for choosing
competitors.source: the vendor's published price list and two client interviews

competitors.packaging: three tiers, audit export only on the top one
competitors.positioning: flexible enough for anything, specific to nothing

market.growth: flat in branch count, rising in approvals per branch as limits fall
market.switchingCost: one migration of open approvals and a retraining day per branch
market.whyBuyersChange: an inspection finding, which is what happened here and is the only trigger anyone named

direction.name: Ledger
direction.rationale: The age of a held payment is the content. Large radii and a wide palette both cost row scannability.

nfr.requirement: the approval queue renders in 800ms at p95
nfr.condition: 500 held payments, on the shared branch terminal over the branch VPN
nfr.measuredBy: a synthetic check against staging every five minutes

nfr.requirement: approval records are kept for 7 years and are not deletable by any product path
nfr.condition: for every payment above the approval limit
nfr.measuredBy: a migration test asserting no DELETE grant on the approvals table

nfr.requirement: every state change records an actor id and a timestamp within 1 second of the action
nfr.condition: on every approval, rejection and release
nfr.measuredBy: an end-to-end test asserting the row exists with a non-null actor

checkDisputes.claim: five interviews per segment, or the shortfall recorded, because below five you are quoting anecdotes with a percentage sign attached
checkDisputes.argument: The compliance director segment is three people in the whole bank and all three were interviewed. Five is not a sample we failed to reach, it is more people than exist. The floor is right for a segment you sample and wrong for one you enumerate, and the check cannot tell those apart from the numbers alone.
